To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
faith leaders and DV advocates can be both helpful and harmful to women with disabilities who are experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV).
women with disabilities who are religious and experience IPV face barriers in seeking and receiving accessible support from faith leaders and domestic abuse shelters.

faith leaders and DV advocates have both strengths and gaps in their responses to IPV survivors with disabilities and that survivors have strengths and gaps in accessing faith communities and domestic violence services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how faith-based communities and domestic violence shelters can better serve women with disabilities of faith backgrounds who are survivors of IPV.
how faith leaders and DV advocates respond to women with disability who are survivors of intimate partner violence and whether their accessibility needs are being met.

the intersectionality of religion, disability, and domestic violence and the need for a more person-centered, trauma-informed approach to the provision of domestic violence services for survivors with disabilities of faith backgrounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the faith communities and DVAs need to work together and with survivors to develop accessible services that meet the needs of WWD of faith backgrounds.
faith communities and DVAs need to work together to create accessible, person-centered, and safe responses for WWD experiencing IPV.
the needs and experiences of women with disabilities are often not being met in the faith-based community and in domestic violence shelters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
faith-based communities and DVAs can be supportive of survivors with disabilities, but they need to be aware of the barriers that WWDs face and how to address them.
the faith-based communities need to be educated on the intersection of IPV and disability and DVAs need to be educated about the intersection of faith and disability. (author abstract)
faith leaders and DVs need to be more aware of disability dynamics in the context of IPV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intersectionality of disability, faith, and domestic violence creates unique barriers to safety for WWD.
survivors of faith backgrounds and disabilities are often not being served by faith leaders and DVAS.
survivors with disabilities of faith backgrounds need to be supported in a person-centered, accessible way by faith leaders and DV advocates.
